refuted_approach: Testing the overlap-gap property via Hamming-distance sets of the full solution space (including free variables) refutes the probe, not the direction: in positive 1-in-3, distance-1 solution pairs exist iff the differing variable is in no clause (S-797c9c8ab6), and #solutions = 2^f * |C| where C is the set of solutions on clause-occurring variables (S-7d35813d05, checked on visible rows of cm-38021e1966ca4346). Hence any interior gap of width <= f is filled by free-variable padding; the 'no gap' readings of cm-df7fbca9ef1a471f and cm-a809f9edb0fb4174 carry no information about solution geometry. Enriched version tried: core-only enumeration (cm-880090181d2a4f15). What remains open: (1) the GJW theorem statement, circuit model and depth bound (source-check impossible in this lab; recorded as QUESTION); (2) whether any density regime of random positive 1-in-3 yields a density-persistent empty overlap window (only finite n<=24 evidence, no persistent gap); (3) whether an overlap gap in a search problem with a polynomial-size unstable algorithm (Gaussian elimination for XOR-SAT) can coexist with circuit lower bounds, i.e. what extra property separates the two.
